name: Red Sea / Suez Canal
summary: Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb, Day 228. A held, pledged, unused chokepoint for neutral shipping and a war zone for Saudi Arabia. The Houthis have held Perim/Mayun since 11 Sep and have not attacked a non-Saudi merchant hull in 32 days (Krieg's test expired unfired; one unattributed near-miss 4 Oct); container lines added Suez services; neutral war-risk fell to 0.2–0.3% while Saudi-linked calls pay 3–7%. Riyadh's ground offensive took Dhubab airfield but not Mayun (AFP 10 Oct). The hinge is a US decision: Trump 'may' join Saudi strikes; the Houthis promise a 'swift and painful' response against US interests if he does — the event most likely to make the strait all-flags.

**No merchant-vessel incident logged in the southern Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb 17–21 Sep (UKMTO/JMIC/Ambrey — negative finding; JMIC September PDF not retrievable).** Kpler: five laden Saudi tankers exited via Bab el-Mandeb in the week. No Red Sea war-risk premium print since July (0.5%+) — the ≥2% trigger is unassessable (GAP). Perim/Mocha held. — no-attack CONFIRMED; pledge RHETORIC.

**Post-Perim week one: the strait is HELD but not CLOSED — no merchant attack logged (UKMTO/Ambrey/JMIC), no post-Perim war-risk print (last Red Sea AWRP 0.5–0.75%, July — the ≥2% trigger cannot be assessed), no container-line suspension citing Perim.** Qatar publicly warned closure would be 'catastrophic for the entire world'; US adviser Boulos: Red Sea freedom of navigation is 'a red line'; Saudi crude that would have loaded at Yanbu is instead moving via Hormuz under US escort (Vortexa), so Red Sea tanker traffic is DOWN by displacement rather than by attack. The Mecca-drone incident (15 Sep) raises the coalition–Houthi temperature on land, not yet at sea. (oprep/UKMTO; Al Jazeera; ToI) — CONFIRMED non-event / REPORTED context.

**A SECOND CHOKEPOINT IS NOW PHYSICALLY HELD BY AN IRANIAN PROXY, AND THE BARRELS IT CARRIES JUST LOST THEIR SOURCE.** Houthi seizure of Perim/Mocha/Dhubab/Hanish (10–11 Sep) gives them the Bab el-Mandeb — ~12% of global trade, 11% of seaborne oil, 8% of LNG — and specifically the Yanbu-to-Asia route whose flows had risen to 8.1 mb/d in Q2 (from 5.4 in Q4-25) as Saudi rerouted around Hormuz. Simultaneously the East-West pipeline feeding Yanbu was shut (11 Sep). Houthi rule: safe for all but Saudi ships; no non-Saudi hit confirmed. Egypt (Suez revenue −60% in 2023–24) maintains 'strategic restraint'; Djibouti received >2,000 Yemenis in 24h; piracy resurgence noted off Somalia (Al Jazeera). Container market NOT repriced (Drewry WCI $4,476/FEU flat 2 wks — box shipping already Cape-routed); Red Sea war-risk was 0.5–0.75% of hull in July — expect repricing (no Sep print). Goldman: +$25 on Brent if Bab el-Mandeb/Suez are disrupted alongside Hormuz. (NBC, AP, AFP, Al Jazeera, Drewry, FinanceFeeds/EIA — CONFIRMED)

Bab el-Mandeb remains OPEN and quiet through 17-19 Jul despite the Iranian instruction's power-infrastructure condition arguably having fired (see houthis). No UKMTO/JMIC incident, no closure move. The strongest independent evidence that the market does not expect closure: the **Suez Canal Authority IMPLEMENTED STEEPER TRANSIT SURCHARGES from 15 July** — laden tankers 25%->37%, ballast 15%->27%, LPG/chemical 20%->32%, dry bulk 10%->22% (more than doubled) — a pricing decision that only makes sense if the Authority expects volumes to hold. Suez revenue is running ~$5.5bn in FY25/26 against the $9.4bn FY22/23 record (-41%), with the SCA guiding to ~$8bn in FY26/27, and Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd are RETURNING to Suez even as they avoid the Gulf — carriers are distinguishing Red Sea risk from Hormuz risk. New adjacent vector: the US Embassy Aqaba threat warning (19 Jul) puts a non-Hormuz Red Sea outlet in play. CONFIRMED.

**A SECOND CHOKEPOINT IS NOW DECLARED BUT NOT ENFORCED.** The Houthis declared a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia on 20 July (see `houthis`). **No vessel has been attacked; ISW-CTP records no Houthi attack on shipping since 7 July; the embargo is enforced by radio turn-back orders only.** The counter-intuitive datum that must travel with this: **Bab el-Mandeb throughput is UP — 7.4m bpd in June versus 4.2m a year earlier** — because Saudi Arabia has been routing crude across the East-West Petroline to Yanbu (loadings ~4m bpd vs ~973k a year earlier) precisely to bypass Hormuz. **The declaration is therefore aimed at the workaround, not at world shipping generally.** Al Jazeera's arithmetic: closing Bab el-Mandeb on top of a shut Hormuz would block **~25% of world oil and gas supply**; Reuters' counter-analysis is that workarounds would limit the impact. **Red Sea war-risk insurance costs rose on the declaration alone** — the first real economic transmission, and it happened on words. Suez: **no traffic or revenue data obtainable this cycle (collection gap)**; the standing datum is that the SCA RAISED surcharges from 15 July, implying it expects volumes to hold. CONFIRMED (declaration) / RHETORIC (enforcement).

The Houthi Saudi-crude embargo produced its first measurable effect — three tankers U-turned (AIS) — but Bab el-Mandeb is OPEN and no vessel has been struck. A sanctioned Iranian rocket-fuel vessel transited the Red Sea freely, underlining that this is targeted coercion of Saudi cargo, not a closure. Tanker equities (Frontline +4.1%) and TTF (+2.8% to a new high) priced a second-chokepoint premium on the declaration. Suez traffic/revenue could not be refreshed this cycle. CONFIRMED (turn-backs) / RHETORIC (closure).

The Houthi Saudi-crude embargo became KINETIC — two Saudi tankers struck, one ablaze (Saudi SPA + UKMTO CONFIRMED). BUT Bab el-Mandeb is NOT closed: ISW counts 30 transits on 22 Jul vs 64 the prior day — a coercive HALVING, not a closure, with >=7 vessels rerouting. A sanctioned Iranian vessel transits freely. Tanker equities did NOT spike (Frontline -1.3%) — the market prices a second-chokepoint premium in oil (Brent ~$97) but not a closure. Suez data could not be refreshed. CONFIRMED (kinetic) / the strait remains OPEN.
